correctness.rationale: The actual RESULT.md at the assigned Git tree fixes flip-versus-rerandomization and hub copying normalization, computes the generator on H sigma_i and sigma_i sigma_j (noise factor −4a), obtains u=bv and v=(m+1)/(m(2b²−1)+1), and derives the reduced (x,h) generator with drift h−bx and hub rate (b−hx)/2. Compactness and uniform polynomial-generator convergence yield stationarity for every subsequential limit. Applying it to x^(k+1) and h*x^k gives E(HX^k)=b M_(k+1) and M_(k+1)=k M_(k−1)/((k+1)b²−1); the compact moment problem uniquely identifies the symmetric beta law and joint hub conditional expectation. All noise a>0 and leaf count m>=2 restrictions in stated correlation are accounted for. Independently solved 12 finite stationary generators and verified exact second moments; those finite instances do not prove the weak limit.
residual_risks: No convergence speed established; stationary not transient mixing. At a=0 finite irreducibility fails; that boundary is excluded.
Independent checks do not prove moment tightness, but compactness and the generator argument in RESULT.md supply it.

value.rationale: The star is a canonical singular-hub graph for which mean-field self-averaging intuition fails at fixed positive noise. A complete compact-support beta stationary law and exact nonvanishing macroscopic variance are natural, independently meaningful probabilistic invariants; the joint hub–leaf profile is not a tiny numerical correction.
residual_risks: Value does not extend automatically to general hub-and-spoke networks or time-dependent noise scaling.

final_claim: For fixed flip rate a>0, a star with unit total copying rate at each vertex has a nondegenerate stationary leaf magnetization X supported on [-1/b,1/b], b=1+2a, such that (1+bX)/2 is Beta((b²−1)/(2b²),(b²−1)/(2b²)); E[H|X]=bX, Var(X)=1/(2b²−1), and the exact finite hub-leaf / distinct-leaf correlation formulas hold.
limitations: Fixed positive flip noise and unit rate of neighbor-copy attempts at every vertex; not noise-free or complete graph.
No limiting mixing times or full total-variation convergence asserted.
